description: One of seven ex-SCADTA W 34s taken over by the Aviación Militar in the 1932 Colombia-Peru war; displayed on floats in the museum pond. Museum's own collection page; photographed at Tocancipá April 2023.
aliases: W 34hi; W34; Junkers W-34; W-34; FAC407; c/n 2823

description: Ex-SCADTA trimotor taken over in 1932-33 (serials 621-626); presidential aircraft of Enrique Olaya Herrera; retired 1950. One of the few unrestored-original Ju 52/3m survivors; on the museum's collection page and photographed March 2024.
aliases: Ju 52/3m; Ju52; Ju-52; Ju 52/3mge; Ju-52/3m; FAC625

description: Sole surviving FAC Thunderbolt of 35 delivered from 1946; the museum page text also gives it as FAC 681, a typo. Wikipedia survivor list identifies it as P-47D-40-RA 45-49102; JetPhotos gives c/n 399-55641. Externally restored by CAMAN; photographed February 2023.

DC-4-1009 built 1946 for SILA/SAS, bought 1954 as presidential aircraft FAC 613 for Gen. Rojas Pinilla, renumbered FAC 690 in 1957, presidential until 1972, retired 1990. Moved from CATAM to Tocancipá by road; museum collection page.

One of six Canadair Sabres (Orenda-engined; museum text calls them Mark IV) delivered 1956 and operated from Palanquero until 1967. Displayed at the Instituto Militar Aeronáutico museum, then at CATAM from 1971; photographed at Tocancipá March 2024.
aliases: CL-13Mk.6; F-86; F-86 Sabre; Sabre Mk.6; Sabre 6; CL-13B; FAC2023; CL13Mk.6; F86; CL13B; CL13

description: One of 14 Mirage 5COA single-seaters delivered 1972 and modernised (canards) from 1988; retired 2010. Posed with the KC-137 Zeus in a simulated refuelling; JetPhotos gives c/n 651. Photographed November 2023.
aliases: Mirage 5COA; Mirage 5COAM; M5-COA; c/n 651; FAC3027

description: Second Mirage at the museum, added by 2022; the museum's own page (Feb 2025) confirms two Mirages at Tocancipá. Serial 3035 sits outside the 3001-3034 block quoted by the museum and needs checking against the airframe. Photographed March 2024.
aliases: Mirage 5COAM; M5-COAM; FAC3035

description: A Kfir is displayed at the museum (visit report of 25 March 2024 photographs it, serial not legible/quoted); the museum's collection pages do not yet list it. Variant and FAC serial unknown - needs reading on site.
aliases: Kfir; Kfir C.2; Kfir C.7; IAI Kfir

description: Ex-Korean Air Lines 707-373C (c/n 19716) delivered December 1983, converted in Israel 1990-91 to KC-137 tanker; retired 2014, dismantled at CATAM and trucked to Tocancipá in October 2018. Largest airframe in the museum; photographed February 2023.

One of eight C-130Bs acquired 1987 (FAC 1006-1013). Trucked from CATAM to the new museum; JetPhotos gives c/n 282-3521 and shows it repainted with fresh titles in January 2022. Photographed February 2023.
Long-time gate guardian at the CATAM entrance, dismantled and moved to Tocancipá in 2017. Museum page says C-47B/D; the 2015 photo essay calls it a DC-3C. USAAF serial not established.
aliases: C-47; C-47B; C47B; DC-3; DC3; Dakota; FAC667; C47

description: One of about 100 Texans (700-series serials) delivered 1940-42; preserved by EMAVI and moved with the museum. JetPhotos c/n 88-16874. Photographed March 2024.
aliases: AT-6D; T-6; T-6D; T6D; T-6 Texan; c/n 88-16874; FAC772; AT6D; T6; AT6

description: Museum page titles it P-80; one of 25 F-80Cs (FAC 2330-2354 per museum text) operated from Palanquero 1955-66, though the painted serial 2061 lies outside that block. Photographed January 2023.

Originally displayed at the Museo Militar in central Bogotá (photographed there 2008); replaced FAC 2033 when the museum moved to Tocancipá, 2033 having stayed at CATAM. JetPhotos c/n 580-8090. Photographed February 2023.
From the first batch of 15 T-37C delivered 1968 (FAC 2100-2114); some directories list it as a T-37B. Photographed November 2023.
aliases: T-37C; T37C; T-37B; Tweety Bird; FAC2112; T37B; T37

description: From the 1980 batch (FAC 2156-2175); operated from Palanquero and later CACOM-3 Barranquilla. Listed by some directories as OA-37B. Photographed January 2023.
aliases: A-37B; A37B; OA-37B; OA37B; FAC2164; A37

description: One of 22 ex-USAF OV-10As acquired 1991 (from FAC 2210); the last five were retired November 2015. Photographed August 2024.
aliases: OV-10A; OV10A; FAC2223; OV10

description: Last of 20 Invaders (FAC 2500-2519) bought 1955, nicknamed chulos for their black paint; retired 1968. Wikipedia survivor list identifies it as A-26C 44-35778. Preserved by CACOM-2; photographed 2015 at CATAM and on the museum page.
One of four Kansans (FAC 901-904) bought 1948, used at Madrid and Techo until 1963; polished natural metal. Photographed February 2023.
aliases: AT-11; AT-11 Kansan; Beech 18; FAC902; AT11

description: Sole Howard 400 built (converted from a PV-1 Ventura, ex-RCAF 2244); later N400MC and YV-183CP, force-landed at Santa Marta, abandoned at Bogotá and taken to the CATAM air park in January 1996. Painted as Lodestar C-60 FAC 654, a false identity; some directories therefore list a Lockheed C-60A at the museum - it is this airframe.
aliases: 400; Howard 400; Howard 500; C-60A; C60A; Lodestar; N400MC; YV-183CP; RCAF 2244; FAC 654; FAC654; YV183CP

description: One of 35 L-20/U-6A Beavers (FAC 101-135, later 5101-5135) delivered 1950, retired 1996; preserved by CACOM-6. 1952-built per the 2015 photo essay. Museum collection page.
aliases: L-20; L-20A; L20A; DHC-2; DHC2; U-6A; FAC108; U6A; L20; U6

description: From the first 50 Mentors delivered 1954 (from FAC 300); the museum lists it simply as T-34, JetPhotos as T-34A c/n CG-120. Photographed April 2023.
One of 30 T-41Ds flown from Wichita to EMAVI in 1968; preserved by EMAVI. JetPhotos c/n R172-0360. Photographed February 2023.

Built 30 May 1977; donated to the FAC by Ecopetrol in December 2001 for pipeline surveillance from the Grupo Aéreo del Casanare, retired 2020. Museum page calls it C-337H; JetPhotos gives 337G c/n 33701792. Photographed August 2024.
Turbo Commander 690 delivered to the FAC in 1986 for VIP and aerial photography work; added to the museum by February 2024. FAC serial not quoted on the museum page.
aliases: 690; Turbo Commander 690; Aero Commander 690; Twin Commander

description: Acquired 1979, latterly the Grupo Aéreo del Caribe's air ambulance; moved from CATAM to the museum in April 2021. JetPhotos c/n LJ-752. Photographed February 2023.
aliases: C90; King Air C90; C-90; c/n LJ-752; FAC5570

description: Bought 1988 for senior-officer and ministerial transport; retired after 31 years and moved from CATAM to the museum in September 2021. JetPhotos c/n 550-0582.
aliases: 550; Citation II; Citation 550; c/n 550-0582; FAC1211

description: One of three Metro/Merlin aircraft acquired 1997 (FAC 1240, 5741, 5742); moved to Tocancipá in 2015. Museum page calls it Merlin C-26; directories give SA227 Metro III.
aliases: C-26B; C26B; SA227; Metro III; FAC1240; C26

description: The FAC's only Arava, nicknamed El Huevito, used from 1968 for tactical transport and parachuting; added to the museum by January 2025 per the museum page.
aliases: Arava201; IAI 201; Arava 201; FAC1952

description: Colombian-built utility aircraft, one of four bought 1998 (FAC 5060-5063) for GAORI; preserved by GAORI. Photographed August 2025.
aliases: 358; Gavilán G-358; G-358; G358; Gavilan 358; FAC5062

description: Colombian-assembled primary trainer (Lancair Legacy derivative) presented at EMAVI in 2017; museum page added January 2023, JetPhotos shows FAC 2440 at the museum February 2023.
aliases: T-90; T-90 Calima; Calima T-90; FAC2440; T90

description: Romanian two-seat glider, one of two (FAC 012/013) received by EMAVI in June 1983 and flown until 2016; JetPhotos identifies the museum example as FAC 013 (April 2023).
aliases: IS28B2; Lark; FAC013; IS28; IS28M2

description: First remotely piloted system operated by the FAC (from 2005); displayed on its launcher in the aircraft park.
aliases: Insitu ScanEagle; ScanEagle; Scan Eagle; FAC6015

description: Represents the first FAC aircraft (three bought 1920 for the Flandes school). Originality not established - the FAC also built a G.III reproduction for EMAVI - treat as a probable reproduction until confirmed on site.
aliases: G.3; Caudron G.III; G.III; G3

description: Curtiss Falcon in 1932-war markings (serials 111-130). No original Colombian Falcon is known to survive; almost certainly a reproduction built for the museum - flagged, needs on-site confirmation.
aliases: F8F; Curtiss Falcon; F8F Falcon; O-1; FAC119; O1

description: Museum page titles it OH-13 FAC 206 (G-model serials 206-214); JetPhotos gives Bell 47G-2 c/n 718. First airframe moved from CATAM to Tocancipá in August 2015. Photographed February 2023.

Painted FAC 220 and so listed by the museum's page title and JetPhotos (c/n 40318); the museum's own text says the museum airframe is FAC 221 and that FAC 220 stands at CACOM-4 Melgar - identity unresolved. Museum page calls it OH-12. Photographed January 2023.
One of ten UH-1Bs acquired from 1963 (from FAC 270, later 4270 series); JetPhotos c/n 461. Photographed February 2023.
aliases: UH-1B; UH1B; Huey; c/n 461; FAC4272; UH1

description: First of 25 Cayuse (FAC 241-265, later 4241-4265) delivered from 1968 to Melgar; JetPhotos lists it as Hughes 369HM c/n 48-0001M. Photographed March 2024.
aliases: OH-6A; OH6A; Hughes 369HM; c/n 48-0001M; FAC4241; OH6

description: Museum page: Defender MD-500 FAC 4251, from the 1985-87 H-500/530 purchases used by CACOM-4 and the volcano-watch service; restored and repainted by CACOM-4 in 2019. Directories list it as Hughes/MD 500E.
One of twelve Enstrom F-28F trainers delivered 1994 to CACOM-4 Melgar; JetPhotos c/n 802. Photographed February 2023.
aliases: F-28F; F28F; Enstrom F28F; c/n 802; FAC4461; F28
